title: Estimation, optimisation, learning
summary: The three algorithm families aimed at finance — what each promises, and the fine print on each.

shots.title:
Three families,
three promises.
shots.subtitle: Almost every quantum-finance paper fits one of them.
shots.narration: Read enough quantum finance papers and they sort into three families. Learn the families and you can place any headline.
Estimation, for pricing and risk. Optimisation, for portfolios and hedging. And learning, for prediction tasks like fills, fraud and credit.

shots.text: **Amplitude estimation** prices by estimating an expected value with error ∝ **1/N** instead of Monte Carlo's **1/√N**.
shots.narration: Family one, estimation. Amplitude estimation computes an expected value, like an option price, with error falling like one over N, instead of Monte Carlo's one over root N.

The idea moved fast on paper: a general Monte Carlo speed-up in 2015, derivative pricing in 2018, value at risk in 2019, tiny demos on hardware in 2020. Then, in 2021, the bill: thousands of error-corrected qubits.

shots.text: **QAOA** and **VQE** tune a short circuit with a classical optimiser. **Annealers** let hardware settle into low-energy answers.
shots.narration: Family two, optimisation. QAOA and VQE tune a short quantum circuit with a classical optimiser. Quantum annealers, like D-Wave's, take another route and let the hardware settle into good answers.

shots.text: The catch: these are **heuristics**. No proof they beat the best classical solvers — and benchmarks find performance depends on depth, parameters and noise.
shots.narration: The catch: these are heuristics. There's no proof they beat the best classical solvers, and benchmarks find that results depend heavily on circuit depth, parameters and noise.

shots.text: **Quantum machine learning** maps data into quantum states and feeds the result to a classical model. Whether it helps depends on the **data**.
shots.narration: Family three, learning. Quantum machine learning maps data into quantum states and passes the result to a classical model. Whether that helps depends heavily on the data.

left.heading: The promise
items: HHL: exponential speed-up for linear systems

right.heading: The fine print
items: Only if input loading, structure and read-out cooperate

shots.narration: And always read the fine print. The famous HHL algorithm promised exponential speed-ups for linear algebra, but only under strict conditions. Some machine-learning speed-ups were later matched by quantum-inspired classical algorithms.

shots.text: Three questions for any claim: **Which family? Which speed-up? Proven or heuristic?**
shots.narration: So for any claim, ask three questions. Which family is it? What speed-up is promised? And is it proven, or a heuristic that still has to win a benchmark?

steps.title: Match the task to the family
steps.brief: A trading floor's wish list. Which algorithm family would a quantum team reach for?

cards.text: Price an exotic derivative by simulating thousands of market paths
cards.why: Pricing by simulation is Monte Carlo — the target of amplitude estimation.

cards.text: Compute Value at Risk for a large portfolio
cards.why: VaR is a probability estimate; Woerner and Egger applied amplitude estimation to it.

cards.text: Choose which 30 bonds to hold under budget and risk limits
cards.why: Discrete selection under constraints is a QUBO — QAOA, VQE-style or annealing.

cards.text: Rebalance holdings while limiting transaction costs
Predict whether a client's bond quote request will be filled
cards.why: A classification problem — HSBC's 2025 trial used quantum-transformed features here.
Classification on data; the quantum role would be a feature map or kernel.

questions.prompt: Amplitude estimation targets which classical technique?
questions.explain: It estimates the same expected value with fewer model evaluations: error ∝ 1/N vs 1/√N.

questions.prompt: QAOA for portfolio optimisation is best described as…
options: A heuristic whose performance depends on depth, parameters and noise
questions.explain: Benchmarks show strong dependence on these factors; no general proof of advantage exists.

questions.prompt: What did Ewin Tang's 2019 result show?
options: A claimed exponential quantum speed-up for recommendations could be matched classically
questions.explain: Her quantum-inspired classical algorithm 'dequantized' a famous quantum machine-learning speed-up.
